claims.text: The baseline coating is elemental Cr deposited on zirconium-alloy cladding by physical vapor deposition.
Elemental Cr coatings can provide protection during normal operation and accident-relevant exposure but can fail prematurely at elevated temperature.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion is responsible for premature failure of the baseline Cr coating.
The proposed intervention is to alloy the Cr coating with approximately 3–5 at.% Al during deposition.
Adding 3–5 at.% Al to Cr will produce finely dispersed, thermodynamically stable Al2O3 at the coating surface and near the Cr/Zr-alloy interface.
Al preferentially oxidizes in the proposed Cr–Al coating.
Preferential oxidation of Al will form a continuous protective Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will impede oxygen diffusion.
The Al2O3 phase will impede interdiffusion of Cr and Zr across the coating/cladding interface.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve coating integrity.
The intrinsic properties of Cr will continue to provide oxidation protection under both normal-operation and accident conditions after Al alloying.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr–Al coating will have lower interfacial Cr–Zr transport.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr–Al coating will have lower oxidation rates and greater oxidation resistance.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr–Al coating will sustain greater mechanical integrity and durability in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
The intervention is applicable during extended exposure to simulated PWR water at approximately 320 °C and 11.3 MPa.
The intervention is applicable during transient steam exposure at approximately 1200 °C.
Uniform Al content must be maintained without forming adverse phases that compromise protection.
Al2O3 offers substantial resistance to high-temperature oxidation and corrosion and grows more slowly than chromia.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.

Comparative Cr and Cr–Al specimens exposed to both environments can separately assess oxidation by mass change and oxide characterization, interfacial transport by EDS profiles, and integrity by adhesion and spallation testing.
